nodes.content: Characterize when staggered policy effects remain partially identifiable under network spillovers and bounded unmeasured adoption confounding.
requirements: Establish assumptions yielding bounds narrower than outcome-range bounds, distinguishing direct effects from spillover effects.
Achieve at least 95% confidence-set coverage uniformly over the stated confounding and interference class.

nodes.content: Use exposure-mapped linear programs under overlap and Γ-bounded adoption odds to separate direct/spillover bounds; invert uniformly calibrated 95% tests.
With Y∈[0,1], four-cell exposure overlap ≥0.1 and Γ≤1.5, direct and neighbor-spillover bounds each narrow [−1,1].
Simulate 10,000 staggered-network panels (Γ≤1.5, overlap≥0.1); compare direct/spillover bound widths against 2 and record minimum confidence-set coverage.
Across 10,000 panels, median direct/spillover bound widths were 1.31/1.57 versus 2; lowest grid-specific empirical coverage was 95.2%.
How can test inversion guarantee 95% coverage across continuous Γ≤1.5 adoption mechanisms, beyond the simulated parameter grid?
Use n3’s worst-covered cells to seed adaptive partitions; derive cellwise worst-case critical values and off-grid corrections for uniform 95% coverage.
Implement interval-arithmetic branch-and-bound to upper-bound rejection probabilities over continuous Γ≤1.5 adoption laws, allocating 0.025 error per effect.
UniformCert v1 exports interval-certified 0.025 per-effect rejection bounds across continuous Γ≤1.5 adoption laws and specified exposure-mapped networks.
Audit UniformCert v1 via exact small-network enumeration and off-grid laws, checking 0.025 rejection certificates and 95% joint coverage.
On 6–10-node networks, exact enumeration corroborated UniformCert v1’s worst-case rejection bounds of ≤0.025 per effect, implying ≥95% joint coverage.
Benchmark clustered and hub-dominated networks at overlap 0.05–0.3, recording separate direct/spillover bound widths and confidence-set coverage.
In 100-node hub networks (overlap 0.1, Γ=1.5), correlated adoption yielded 91.4% joint coverage despite certified 95%.
Which restrictions on correlated adoption restore ≥95% joint coverage in hub networks without widening direct and spillover bounds to [−1,1]?
Extend n9’s certificates given n11’s failure: assume independent hub-block shocks, Γ-bounded adoption; certify 95% joint coverage and sub-2 direct/spillover widths.
Implement block-factorized worst-case calibration; benchmark 100-node hub panels under independent versus shared block shocks, measuring joint coverage and direct/spillover widths.
HubBlockCert v2 contains block-factorized calibration, independent-block shock specifications, and reproducible direct/spillover width and joint-coverage benchmarks.
Combine Γ-sensitive difference-in-differences and bounded trend violations with independent-block test inversion for joint 95% direct/spillover bounds.
Under independent hub-block shocks, Γ≤1.5, and ≤0.1 trend drift, sensitivity-DiD yields ≥95% joint coverage and sub-2 direct/spillover widths.
Using HubBlockCert v2, simulate 10,000 independent-block hub panels and certify worst-case joint coverage and direct/spillover widths across Γ≤1.5, drift≤0.1.
HubBlockCert v2 certified ≥95% joint coverage uniformly over Γ≤1.5, drift≤0.1; 10,000 independent-block panels had maximal direct/spillover widths 1.82/1.91.
Using HubBlockCert v2, vary cross-block shock correlation (ρ=0–0.2) at Γ=1.5, drift=0.1; measure joint coverage and direct/spillover widths.
At ρ=0, within-block correlated adoption (Γ=1.5, drift=0.1) yielded 93.8% joint coverage despite independent block shocks.
Does HubBlockCert v2 bound within-block joint adoption dependence or only individual odds, explaining the 93.8% coverage failure?
Reconcile n18’s certificate with n20’s failure by auditing within-block adoption likelihoods, then impose a joint Γ-block cap and recertify.
Reproduce n18/n20 at ρ=0; enumerate within-block adoption laws under marginal versus joint Γ≤1.5 caps, recalculating worst-case joint coverage.
Exact enumeration at ρ=0: marginal Γ≤1.5 permits within-block adoption dependence and 93.8% coverage; a joint cap restores ≥95%.
With joint block-adoption likelihood ratios ≤1.5, independent blocks, overlap≥0.1, and drift≤0.1, sensitivity-DiD attains ≥95% joint coverage and sub-2 direct/spillover widths.
Extend n24’s enumeration to certify ≥95% joint coverage and sub-2 direct/spillover widths uniformly under joint Γ≤1.5, independent blocks, overlap≥0.1, drift≤0.1.
Certified ≥95% joint coverage and maximal direct/spillover widths of 1.88/1.95 uniformly over independent blocks, joint Γ≤1.5, overlap≥0.1, drift≤0.1.
Adopt joint Γ≤1.5 block caps: marginal calibration yielded 93.8% coverage despite initial certification; revised bounds certify ≥95%, widths 1.88/1.95.
Use relevant randomized rollout instruments for direct/spillover effects; bound exclusion violations and invert Bonferroni tests for joint 95% coverage.
Randomized own/neighbor instruments (singular value ≥0.2, exclusion bias ≤0.05) yield sub-2 direct/spillover bounds and ≥95% joint coverage despite correlated adoption.
Invert randomization tests in 10,000 hub-network rollouts; evaluate joint coverage and direct/spillover widths under correlated adoption, strength≥0.2, bias≤0.05.
Across 10,000 correlated-adoption hub rollouts, minimum scenario joint coverage was 95.3%; median direct/spillover widths were 1.42/1.68 versus 2.
Enumerate 8-node randomized rollouts near instrument strength 0.2; maximize joint rejection over correlated adoption and exclusion bias ≤0.05.
At strength 0.2 and bias 0.05, exact enumeration found 92.4% joint coverage; point-null inversion ignored composite exposure uncertainty.
Can composite-null randomization tests account for exposure uncertainty while retaining ≥95% joint coverage and sub-2 bounds at instrument strength 0.2?
Reconcile n31/n33: maximize composite-null randomization p-values over exposures and bias≤0.05; Bonferroni-invert, certify 95% coverage, assess widths at strength≥0.2.
Reanalyze n31/n33 with composite-null exposure and bias≤0.05 maximization; measure direct/spillover widths and certify joint coverage at strength≥0.2.
At strength 0.2, composite-null inversion certified ≥95% joint coverage, but direct/spillover widths reached 1.76/2.00, losing spillover identification.
Defer rollout-IV at strength 0.2: simulated 95.3% coverage masked 92.4% exact coverage; corrected spillover width equals 2.
Require rollout-IV strength≥0.35 and exclusion bias≤0.05; invert worst-case composite-null randomization tests for separate direct/spillover bounds with uniform 95% coverage.
At strength≥0.35 and exclusion bias≤0.05, composite-null inversion yields sub-2 direct/spillover widths and uniform ≥95% joint coverage under correlated adoption.
Certify worst-case joint rejection and maximal direct/spillover widths via composite-null enumeration over correlated adoption and exposure mappings, strength≥0.35, bias≤0.05.
Composite-null enumeration certified ≤5% joint rejection and maximal direct/spillover widths 1.72/1.94 under correlated adoption, strength≥0.35, bias≤0.05.
Extend n41’s certificates cohortwise; report direct/spillover bounds only where instrument strength≥0.35 and worst-case joint rejection≤5%.
Implement cohort-stratified composite-null inversion with 0.05/(2K) tests across K rollout cohorts, auditing strength≥0.35 and direct/spillover widths.
CohortIVCert v1 outputs cohort-specific direct/spillover intervals, ≥0.35 strength flags, width diagnostics, and Bonferroni 95% joint-coverage certificates.
Audit CohortIVCert v1 across four staggered cohorts: enumerate correlated-adoption laws, verify joint coverage certificates, strength flags, and direct/spillover widths.
Four-cohort enumeration certified ≥95% joint coverage under admissible correlated adoption; maximal direct/spillover widths were 1.89/1.98, with strengths≥0.35.
Adopt strength≥0.35 cohortwise rollout-IV: n41/n46 certify ≥95% joint coverage and sub-2 direct/spillover widths despite correlated adoption.
